metadata.icdo_version: ICD-O-3.2. morphology_entries[] is GENERATED by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group VI from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite, run via build/generate_group06_entries.py, never transcribed from the REDCap option file or the diagnostic pathway document (Group 6 build contract §1, §0.3). Generator summary, 22 September 2026: ICCC range entries 160, distinct codes 160, absent at the declared behaviour (3) 70, usable 90, (code,behaviour) records 90 -- all five numbers match the contract's own pre-verified figures exactly. 'Absent at the declared behaviour' means absent at behaviour 3, not absent from ICD-O-3.2 altogether -- the same wording trap recorded in the Group 5 metadata for 9514, and in Group 4 for 8683 (contract §0.3). Eleven of those 70 absent-at-behaviour-3 codes are REDCap options the tool cannot emit (contract §2A) -- ten behaviour exclusions and one deleted number, the first retired ICD-O-3.2 number this project has met in a live REDCap option list: 8965 Nephrogenic adenofibroma -- DELETED in ICD-O-3.2 (IARC 'Deleted codes and their terms', 9 Oct 2020); moved to 9013/0, zero rows for 8965 in icdo32.sqlite. 8966 Renomedullary interstitial cell tumor -- behaviour 0 only; Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places it at 8966/0. 8967 Ossifying renal tumor -- behaviour 0 only; Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places ossifying renal tumour of infancy at 8967/0. 8325 Metanephric adenoma -- behaviour 0 only; Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places it at 8325/0. 8361 Juxtaglomerular tumor -- behaviour 0 only; Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places it at 8361/0. 9013 Adenofibroma, NOS -- behaviour 0 only; Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places metanephric adenofibroma at 9013/0. 8040 Small cell carcinoma, NOS (REDCap's label) -- mislabelled and out of behaviour: ICD-O-3.2's 8040 is 'Tumorlet' at behaviours 0 and 1 only; the entity REDCap's label names, small cell carcinoma NOS, is actually 8041/3, offered separately in the same REDCap list and built as a Tier B entry in this file. 8053 Squamous cell papilloma, inverted -- behaviour 0 only. 8060 Squamous papillomatosis -- behaviour 0 only. 8191 Embryonal adenoma -- behaviour 0 only. 8561 Adenolymphoma -- behaviour 0 only. The test applied throughout is the one Jay's ruling and the Group 3/4/5 contracts already establish: a code leaves the decision tree only when no current WHO entity lives on its stem at the group's declared behaviour, never merely because ICD-O-3.2 prints no usable term at some OTHER behaviour (contract §0.6). Full detail, including the three ICD-O-3.2 additions the inventory carries that REDCap does not (8023, 8054, 8482) and the eight REDCap-string drifts the exact-string check is expected to report, is in the Group 6 build contract §2 and, for the REDCap-facing repair package, in docs/group_06_layer1_repair.md (not authored by this task).

ICD-O-3.2 preferred term 'Neoplasm, malignant', behaviour 3, no [obs] marker; synonyms 'Blastoma, NOS', 'Tumor, malignant, NOS', 'Cancer', 'Malignancy', 'Unclassified tumor, malignant'. This is the group-wide fallback under Visser rule 5: Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rule 5 -- anything not in the paper's Table 3 or Table 4, diagnosed without pathology, is 8000/3, unless a coding expert at the registry rules otherwise (contract §0.11 point 3). A renal mass that fails the nephroblastoma imaging constellation (contract §4.2) and has no tissue in the file is 8000/3 at C64.9, ICCC-3 subgroup VIc -- that is what VIc is for. ★ Router status, contract §3.4 -- CLOSED during this build by a concurrent commit, not by this script: data/shared/presentation_router.json's dual_group_rules['8000-8005'] now carries a 'C64.9' -> {group: 6, subgroup: 'VIc'} branch, listed above the Group XII default, using the 'topography_in' shape app.js's branchMatches() actually reads (commit d205d79, 'Four router branches were dead, two of them across a group boundary', 22 Sep 2026 -- the same commit found and fixed the related dead-branch defect on 8963, recorded on that entry's topography_routing_note). A malignant renal neoplasm NOS can now reach Group VI through the router; group_id 6 in presentation_router.json's own groups map still reads built: false with no tree, so the clerk-facing path through a Group VI document_inventory gate is not yet wired end-to-end -- that remains the next task's work, not a router gap. Cancer 2003;97(9):2318-2326 defines nuclear unrest -- nuclear enlargement resembling anaplasia with no abnormal multipolar mitotic figures -- as favourable histology, not anaplasia; Pfister SM, et al. Cancer Discovery 2022;12(2):331-355 gives the WHO three-part true-anaplasia criterion (nucleomegaly at least three times normal, hyperchromatism, abnormal/atypical mitoses); both stay 8960/3, and the words 'atypia' or 'nuclear enlargement' alone must never set a high-risk flag. The SIOP risk subtypes (completely necrotic, blastemal, regressive, epithelial, stromal, mixed, focal or diffuse anaplasia -- Vujanić GM, et al. Medical and Pediatric Oncology 2002;38(2):79-82) are likewise code-neutral. ★ Registrar correction (contract §3.3, §5.3): the diagnostic pathway document asserts congenital mesoblastic nephroma is recoded to 8960 'by registry convention', citing no source. WHO 2022 Table 1 and ICD-O-3.2 agree that mesoblastic nephroma, and its classic, cellular and mixed subtypes, sit at 8960/1 -- behaviour 1, outside this group's behaviour-3 declaration. Coding a congenital mesoblastic nephroma as 8960/3 would record a malignant Wilms tumour for an infant with a borderline fibroblastic tumour. This build refuses the recode; congenital mesoblastic nephroma is a behaviour_exclusion on 8960/1 for the next task's tree, not a recode here, and if the registrar wants the recode it needs an explicit ruling (contract §11.2). Evidence does not monotonically refine this code (contract §4.1): histology, when it exists, arrives after the nephrectomy that treats the child and refines the SIOP risk group, not the ICD-O code -- 8960/3 is the code at every stage, and the tool must not present missing histology as outstanding workup on this code (Spreafico F, et al. Nature Reviews Disease Primers 2021;7:75).

nodes.question: A child with a suspected renal (kidney) tumour. What is actually in this patient's file?
nodes.hint: Under SIOP protocols, up-front chemotherapy without a prior biopsy is standard for a typical Wilms tumour presentation, so a histology report often does not exist yet at the point of coding — that is expected, not a gap to chase.
nodes.coding_note: Tree architecture per build contract §4. Five routes off this node, matching the Group 5 rb_document_inventory idiom (contract §4, Group 5 build contract §4). Unlike Group 5, the histology route passes through rn_age_gate before rn_histology, because the SMARCB1/INI1 fork at rn_ihc_checklist needs a precise age band (contract §4.3); the imaging and inadequate-specimen routes go directly to rn_imaging_pathway without the numeric gate — see rn_imaging_pathway's own coding_note for why (deviation from the contract's literal diagram, recorded there and in the build report). primary_site is captured 'C64.9' on every option because this whole tree is entered specifically for a kidney mass (tree-level topography declaration) — captured explicitly here, rather than assumed, so rn_ihc_checklist's 8963 (rhabdoid tumour of the kidney) rule can carry its own per-rule 'when' confirming C64.9, which check_group6_8963_topography requires (contract §3.1, §0.2: 8963 at a CNS or soft-tissue site is a different ICCC-3 group entirely).

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no imaging report, no cytology, no histology report in the file
Ultrasound, CT, or MRI report — no tissue (cytology or histology) in the file
Histology report from a nephrectomy, core biopsy, or intraoperative specimen
Fine-needle aspiration or other cytology report only — no histology report in the file
A specimen (cytology, or biopsy/nephrectomy) was obtained but is reported INADEQUATE, non-diagnostic, or technically UNINTERPRETABLE

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: This node never emits a code. Visser 2023 Table 3 (pp. 04–05) gives nephroblastoma basis 2 — clinical investigation, including imaging — not ‘1 or 2’ the way Group V's retinoblastoma row reads. A referral letter or clinical note alone, however strongly worded, cannot register a code in this group.
nodes.coding_note: The deliberate difference from Group 5's rb_clinical_alias (build contract, non-negotiables list): rb_clinical_alias has a basis-1 option because Visser gives retinoblastoma '1 or 2'. Nephroblastoma is basis 2 only (contract §0.11, §4.2), so no option on this node may carry a morphology_code — both options route onward or exclude. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05; rule 4, p. 03 ('possible is not registrable').

options.label: Note states or strongly suspects a renal or Wilms tumour, or describes a palpable abdominal mass, haematuria, or a similar finding consistent with a renal malignancy
options.reason: Nephroblastoma is registrable at basis 2 (clinical investigation, including imaging) and no lower. A referral letter or clinical note alone, with no imaging and no tissue, cannot register a code in this group yet. The wording is recorded and the case proceeds to the imaging constellation.

options.label: Note describes nonspecific findings, or a differential that includes a non-malignant cause (for example a simple renal cyst, urinary tract infection, or hydronephrosis) that could equally explain them
options.reason: A non-malignant disorder could equally explain these findings. Under Visser 2023 rule 4 (p. 03), the case is not registered at all in the absence of imaging or pathology.

nodes.question: What does the fine-needle aspiration or other cytology report show?
nodes.hint: A cytology cannot grade differentiation, establish a growth pattern, or reliably separate nephroblastoma from the other small round cell tumours of childhood — record it as Nephroblastoma, NOS only, never a subtype, and only where the smear is specifically diagnostic.
nodes.coding_note: ENCR basis 5 for cytology, general vocabulary (not group-specific): Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 1, p. 03 — the same citation Group 5's rb_cytology uses for the identical fact. No Group VI-specific source states a cytology basis for nephroblastoma; this is the general ENCR basis-of-diagnosis scale, applied here as it is applied in Group 5.

options.label: Cytology shows a small round blue cell tumour with a triphasic (blastemal, epithelial, stromal) pattern, or is otherwise specifically diagnostic of nephroblastoma — no tissue available to subtype further
options.reason: Cells diagnostic of nephroblastoma are present on cytology, at European Network of Cancer Registries basis of diagnosis 5. A cytology cannot grade differentiation or establish a growth pattern, so this is recorded as Nephroblastoma, NOS (8960/3), never a subtype.
options.coding_note: satisfies_tests ['Imaging','Histology'] added: 8960's generated entry requires BOTH in diagnostic_tests_required. A diagnostic cytology is stronger evidence (ENCR basis 5) than the imaging constellation (basis 2), so imaging is not outstanding on a case that already has cells. Histology is suppressed for the same reason it is suppressed on rn_imaging_pathway's own terminal (contract §4.1): under SIOP a nephrectomy specimen is a later TREATMENT step, not a diagnostic gap this cytology-confirmed case is missing — printing it as outstanding would invite the same false 'more specific code' claim the Group 5 build report records and fixes for 9510.

options.label: Cytology is non-diagnostic, shows scant or insufficient material, or the pattern is not specific for nephroblastoma and could equally represent another small round cell tumour of childhood
options.reason: The cytology did not show findings specific for nephroblastoma. This cannot be registered as Nephroblastoma, NOS. Recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) — this group's own unspecified-malignant subgroup (VIc) at C64.9, not a referral to a different group — pending a diagnostic specimen.

nodes.question: Patient's age at diagnosis, in completed years?
nodes.hint: Tick 'not documented' rather than guessing. This step only captures the age band for the differential ahead — it does not by itself change any code.
nodes.coding_note: Non-negotiable per build contract, task brief: numeric_gate, variable patient_age_years, unit years, band_variable age_band, bands <2 · 2-4 · 5-9 · >=10 · not_documented, nos_fallback 8000 (§0.11, Visser rule 5). All five bands share next_node rn_histology ('bands may share a next_node; the gate's job is capture') — the age value itself does not choose a different downstream node, it is read later by rn_ihc_checklist's resolution_logic ('when': {'age_band': [...]})  for the SMARCB1/INI1 fork (contract §4.3). DEVIATION, recorded per the contract's own invitation ('a deviation is allowed if it is recorded with its reason'): the contract's §4 diagram draws this same box feeding both rn_imaging_pathway and rn_histology. app.js's numeric_gate resolves through exactly one next_node per band (resolveNode(), 'numeric_gate' case) or one override_when per captured-variable match (checked before bands, and an override does not set band_variable/range — confirmed by reading app.js's override branch at resolveNode() before authoring this node) — there is no mechanism for one gate to fan out to two different downstream nodes by entry route while still setting age_band correctly for both. Since precise age banding is load-bearing only for the SMARCB1/INI1 fork (rn_ihc_checklist), not for the imaging route, this gate is entered only from the histology route (rn_document_inventory's histology option, and rn_imaging_insufficient's 'histology now in the file' option). The imaging route's own age criterion is captured instead as diversion_criteria item 6 on rn_imaging_pathway, in plain text — which matches the contract's own framing of that threshold as 'under revision' and 'authored as a diversion, not as a hard cut-off' (§4.2), and matches the Group 4 precedent (sa_imaging_neuroblastoma's 'Age 5 years or older' diversion checkbox, no separate numeric_gate).

bands.coding_note: Typical rhabdoid tumour of the kidney window (contract §4.3 rule 2).
Still within the rhabdoid tumour of the kidney window (contract §4.3 rule 2).

Matches neither the rhabdoid window (<5) nor the renal medullary carcinoma window (>=10) — falls to rn_ihc_checklist's unconditioned SMARCB1-loss rule if reached, never auto-assigned to either specific code.
Renal medullary carcinoma / ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma window (contract §4.3 rule 1); also the age at which the imaging route's diversion criterion 6 forces tissue.
Age not documented — the SMARCB1/INI1 fork's age-conditioned rules cannot fire; falls to the unconditioned rule or the node's own nos_fallback if SMARCB1 is also untested.

nos_fallback.name: Neoplasm, malignant
nos_fallback.reason: Age capture step; every band above already advances to the histology differential, so this fallback is not expected to fire. If reached, coded to Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) pending registrar review, per Visser 2023 rule 5 (p. 03).

nodes.question: No tissue exists. Tick every feature the ultrasound, CT, or MRI report actually states, then answer the diversion checklist below.
nodes.hint: Both features must be genuinely stated in the report for the constellation to count — do not infer either one. Spreafico 2021 (PDF p. 10): SIOP's own algorithm still recommends tissue in patients aged 7 or older, or with any of the imaging features listed below; that age threshold is under revision, which is why age is asked as a diversion question rather than built into the constellation itself.
nodes.coding_note: imaging_sufficient: true on 8960/3 only (contract §0.11, §4.2); basis_of_diagnosis 2, never 1, per Visser 2023 Table 3, pp. 04-05. Engine constraint (contract §0.6, docs/TODO.md §10, task brief fact 1): imagingPathway() renders only imaging_features, biochemical_questions and diversion_criteria — options[] is never rendered, so this node declares insufficient_next_node, no options[], and carries its own morphology_code/behavior_code/basis_of_diagnosis. Imaging features are read off contract §4.2 ('intrarenal origin — the claw sign'; 'a large, well-demarcated mass that pushes rather than invades'); the age qualifier the contract attaches to the second feature is deliberately NOT folded into these checkboxes (engine fact 8, delivered mid-build) — imaging_features render as an AND-gated checklist (app.js line ~2275, .every()), so a compound item would make the whole route unreachable on a report that states everything except age, and age is already covered, more honestly, by diversion criterion 6. The dedicated imaging source (Chung EM et al., RadioGraphics 2016/2017) is not on disk (contract §4.2); these two features rest on Spreafico 2021 and the papers index, and both Chung papers belong on docs/sources-requested.md (out of scope for this file). Diversion criteria: items 1-4 and 5 are SIOP's own atypical-imaging indications plus the nephrogenic-rests exclusion (contract §4.2, citing Spreafico 2021 PDF p. 10 verbatim and Fialkowski E et al. 2023 for §3.5); item 6 is the age/medullary-pattern criterion, authored as a soft diversion because the age threshold is explicitly 'under revision' (contract §4.2 point 6). satisfies_tests ['Histology'] is not optional: build contract §4.1 states in terms this exact case — 'the 8960 terminal must NOT present missing histology as an outstanding-workup row the clerk should close. Nothing is outstanding: under SIOP the tissue does not exist yet, and under COG a biopsy would upstage the tumour to local stage III.' Without it, 8960's generated entry (diagnostic_tests_required ['Imaging','Histology']) makes the workup panel print a 'Histology — pending' row on this group's own modal path — the same defect the Group 5 build report records and fixes for 9510 ('inviting a contraindicated procedure'). Found driving this branch in the browser before this fix was added.
imaging_features: Intrarenal mass with a claw sign of compressed renal parenchyma at its margin
Well-demarcated mass that displaces (pushes) adjacent vessels and structures rather than encasing or invading them

diversion_criteria.reason: A SIOP atypical-imaging feature. Spreafico 2021 (PDF p. 10): SIOP's algorithm recommends a percutaneous image-guided core needle biopsy for this finding. Tissue is required rather than coding on imaging alone.
A SIOP atypical-imaging feature (Spreafico 2021, PDF p. 10). Tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: Vessel encasement, rather than displacement, by the mass
diversion_criteria.reason: A SIOP atypical-imaging feature (Spreafico 2021, PDF p. 10), and the same finding that separates neuroblastoma — which encases vessels and is extrarenal — from Wilms tumour, which displaces them. A case with true vessel encasement needs tissue, and may belong in Group IV, not Group VI.
A SIOP atypical-imaging feature (Spreafico 2021, PDF p. 10). Tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: Diffuse or multifocal renal involvement, or nephrogenic rests / nephroblastomatosis described
diversion_criteria.reason: No test — imaging or pathology — reliably separates nephrogenic rests or nephroblastomatosis from Wilms tumour (Fialkowski E, et al., Pediatric Blood & Cancer 2023;70(Suppl. 2):e30162). This is not auto-coded to Nephroblastoma, NOS on imaging alone.

diversion_criteria.feature: Child is ten years of age or older, or the mass has an infiltrative medullary pattern
diversion_criteria.reason: Renal cell carcinoma overtakes Wilms tumour in the second decade of life (Cajaiba MM, et al., Cancer 2018;124(16):3381-3389), and imaging alone cannot carry a carcinoma diagnosis. This threshold is under revision in the SIOP literature, which is why it is asked as a diversion rather than built into the imaging constellation.

nodes.upgrade_path: A tissue diagnosis would confirm nephroblastoma histologically, allow anaplasia and SIOP risk grouping to be recorded, and exclude the rhabdoid tumour, clear cell sarcoma, and renal cell carcinoma differentials — but under SIOP, tissue does not exist yet at this stage, and requesting it is not an outstanding-workup item on the modal path (contract §4.1).

nodes.step_label: Imaging did not confirm — what next
nodes.question: The imaging constellation did not confirm nephroblastoma — either a diversion criterion applies or a required feature is missing. What does the file show?
nodes.hint: A diversion criterion sends the case to tissue because SIOP's own algorithm calls for it there — it does not mean tissue will settle the question. Spreafico 2021 (PDF p. 10): needle biopsy cannot reliably distinguish Wilms tumour from nephrogenic rests, and often misses anaplasia. Do not treat a pending biopsy as a formality.
nodes.coding_note: Reached only from rn_imaging_pathway's insufficient_next_node. Build contract task brief, engine fact 1 and §4.2: the node the diversion leads to must not imply a core biopsy settles the question — the hint above carries that, and no option here claims tissue will resolve the case with certainty. Diffuse/multifocal or nephrogenic-rests findings route to non_reportable per §3.5, never to a pending-workup code, because no test separates them from Wilms tumour and a diffuse process with no discrete tumour is not registrable on imaging alone. The other atypical-imaging diversions emit this group's OWN 8000/3 (VIc, malignant neoplasm NOS at C64.9) rather than referring to Group XII — the build's check_group6-style routing check rejects a refer_group destination naming a code this group already owns outright and is not topography_dependent, which 8000 is (contract §0.2 subgroup VIc). This corrected an initial authoring pass that mirrored Group 5's rb_imaging_insufficient (which correctly uses refer_group because Group V does not own 8000 at all) without checking Group VI's own inventory first. The two 'tissue has since been obtained' options both UNION 'Imaging' into evidence_tests alongside the new tissue type — found auditing every terminal's diagnostic_tests_required against its accumulated evidence_tests (mirroring app.js finish()'s missing-test computation): without this, a clerk who reaches this node via real imaging and then supplies histology would see 8960/3's required Imaging test printed as falsely outstanding downstream, because app.js's fallbackTarget() (used for every hop off an unresolved imaging_pathway) carries no captures of its own and this was the only JSON-level place left to restore it.

options.label: Findings match one or more SIOP atypical-imaging features — psoas infiltration, numerous calcifications, vessel encasement, or massive lymphadenopathy — or the child is ten years of age or older, or the mass has an infiltrative medullary pattern. No tissue yet in the file
options.reason: This cannot be registered as Nephroblastoma, NOS on the imaging constellation alone. SIOP's own algorithm indicates a needle biopsy for this finding, but a needle biopsy is not a guarantee the case will be fully resolved (Spreafico 2021, PDF p. 10; see this step's hint). Recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) — this group's own unspecified-malignant subgroup (VIc) at C64.9 — pending a diagnostic specimen.
options.coding_note: satisfies_tests ['Imaging'] declared unconditionally: reaching this option means an actual ultrasound/CT/MRI report was reviewed against the SIOP atypical-feature checklist, regardless of which rn_document_inventory route the case entered by (found in the browser: rn_imaging_pathway's own insufficient_next_node hop carries no captures of its own — app.js's fallbackTarget() returns only {next_node}, so a case that reached this node via rn_clinical_alias's referral route, whose evidence_tests still reads 'Referral only', would otherwise show 8000's required Imaging test as falsely outstanding on a branch that is itself imaging-based).

options.label: Diffuse or multifocal renal involvement is described, or the report specifically describes nephrogenic rests (perilobar or intralobar) or nephroblastomatosis, with no discrete malignant mass identified anywhere
options.reason: No test — imaging or pathology — reliably separates nephrogenic rests or nephroblastomatosis from Wilms tumour (Fialkowski E, et al., Pediatric Blood & Cancer 2023;70(Suppl. 2):e30162). With no discrete tumour identified, this is not coded as Nephroblastoma, NOS and is not registered.

options.label: Tissue has since been obtained — a cytology or fine-needle aspiration report is now in the file
Tissue has since been obtained — a histology report (nephrectomy, biopsy, or intraoperative specimen) is now in the file

nodes.question: What does the histology report describe?
nodes.hint: Code from the report's own stated pattern — do not infer architecture or a specific carcinoma subtype yourself. Anaplasia and SIOP risk grouping (completely necrotic, blastemal, epithelial, stromal, mixed, focal or diffuse anaplasia) do not change the code: every nephroblastoma pattern stays 8960/3 regardless of grade or risk group (contract §4.4). A report saying 'atypia' or 'nuclear enlargement' alone, with nothing about abnormal mitotic figures, does not support anaplasia — Vujanić 2002 (p. 81) requires all three of atypical tri-/multipolar mitoses, marked nuclear enlargement (at least three times adjacent cells), and hyperchromatic nuclei together.
nodes.coding_note: Wilms-vs-non-Wilms differential per build contract §4 architecture diagram. DEVIATION, recorded: the contract lists only 'rhabdoid morphology' and 'clear-cell-sarcoma morphology' as the two routes into rn_ihc_checklist. A third route is added here — poorly differentiated/undifferentiated carcinoma or a medullary growth pattern — because §4.3's own instruction to include ALK in that node's panel only makes clinical sense if a medullary-pattern carcinoma can actually reach it: renal medullary carcinoma and ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma present as carcinoma morphology, not as rhabdoid or clear-cell-sarcoma morphology, and rn_carcinoma's own leaf options have no mechanism to test SMARCB1 or ALK. Anaplasia/SIOP risk criteria: Vujanić GM, et al. Medical and Pediatric Oncology 2002;38(2):79-82, Table I, p. 81. Hill DA, et al. Cancer 2003;97(9):2318-2326 (nuclear unrest, favourable, not anaplasia). Pfister SM, et al. Cancer Discovery 2022;12(2):331-355 (WHO three-part anaplasia criterion). No dedicated SIOP-risk capture node is built in this tree — scope decision recorded in the build report — the code-neutrality instruction is carried in this node's hint instead, since every nephroblastoma pattern below resolves to the same 8960/3 regardless of risk group.

options.label: Nephroblastoma (Wilms tumour) morphology — blastemal, epithelial and/or stromal elements in any combination or proportion, with no cystic change, no rhabdoid or clear-cell-sarcoma pattern, and no carcinomatous architecture described
options.reason: Triphasic or other nephroblastoma morphology on histology. Recorded as Nephroblastoma, NOS (8960/3) regardless of which elements predominate, and regardless of anaplasia status or SIOP risk group, which are prognostic and code-neutral (contract §4.4).
options.coding_note: satisfies_tests ['Imaging'] added: 8960's generated entry requires BOTH Imaging and Histology in diagnostic_tests_required, so a case reached by histology alone (evidence_tests=['Histology']) would otherwise show Imaging as outstanding and print the engine's automatic 'Imaging would yield a more specific code' line — false on a specimen already histologically confirmed as nephroblastoma (the same defect the Group 5 build report records and fixes for 9510).

options.label: Cystic renal mass — a mass composed predominantly or entirely of cysts, or a nephroblastoma with prominent cystic change
Small round blue cell tumour with rhabdoid features — eccentric nuclei, prominent nucleoli, eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions
Small round or spindle cell tumour with a clear cell sarcoma of the kidney pattern — cords or nests of cells with clear-to-pale cytoplasm and a delicate ('chicken-wire') capillary network
Poorly differentiated or undifferentiated carcinoma, or a medullary growth pattern — sheets or a reticular/cribriform architecture with a prominent desmoplastic stroma, centred in the renal medulla
Other carcinomatous / adenocarcinomatous architecture — glandular, papillary, clear cell, chromophobe, or solid epithelial pattern not matching the medullary pattern above

Mesoblastic nephroma morphology — a spindle cell (fibroblastic/myofibroblastic) proliferation infiltrating renal parenchyma, classic, cellular, or mixed subtype, with NO nephroblastoma component described anywhere

behaviour_exclusion.reason: Mesoblastic nephroma is a borderline fibroblastic tumour of infancy, coded 8960/1 in both ICD-O-3.2 and WHO 2022. ICCC-3 Group VI admits behaviour 3 only, so it is not a registrable cancer in this group and no Group VI code is emitted for it — it is not recoded to 8960/3. Record the finding and refer the case to the registrar.

options.label: Diffuse or multifocal nephrogenic rests (perilobar or intralobar), or nephroblastomatosis, with NO discrete nephroblastoma component described anywhere
options.reason: No test — imaging or pathology — reliably separates nephrogenic rests or nephroblastomatosis from Wilms tumour (Fialkowski E, et al., Pediatric Blood & Cancer 2023;70(Suppl. 2):e30162). WHO 2022 Table 1 lists nephrogenic rests and nephroblastomatosis with no ICD-O code against any of them. With no discrete tumour identified, this is not registered.

options.label: Report wording does not clearly match any of the above

nodes.question: What does the file record about this child's sickle-cell status?
nodes.hint: 'Unknown' is not the same as tested-and-negative, and in this registry it will often be the modal answer — record it as its own state rather than defaulting to negative.
nodes.coding_note: Captures sickle_cell_status for rn_ihc_checklist's SMARCB1/INI1 fork (contract §4.3). DEVIATION, recorded: an earlier pass captured this via test_result_states directly on rn_ihc_checklist, but that mechanism's states are a closed, test-outcome vocabulary (adequate/failed/inadequate/negative/not_assessable/not_available/not_done/not_indicated/positive per build/build_database.py's own check) that has no room for 'trait' or 'disease' — sickle-cell status is a clinical/haematological state, not a test result. A small document_inventory node, inserted between rn_histology (and rn_cystic's own unclear catch-all) and rn_ihc_checklist, is the closed-vocabulary-compliant way to capture it: four plain options, each captures sickle_cell_status and advances to rn_ihc_checklist.

nodes.question: What does the histology report state about this cystic renal mass?
nodes.hint: 8959 is one four-digit code spanning three different diseases at three different behaviours — only the malignant one, /3, belongs in this group. Read the report's own wording carefully: a cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma is a real, SIOP low-risk paediatric diagnosis, not a lesser finding, even though this group cannot code it.
nodes.coding_note: Build contract §3.2, non-negotiables list. Four outcomes on the 8959 stem: /3 malignant cystic nephroma is emitted (WHO 2022 Table 1 lists no entity on 8959/3 at all — the code is retained on ICD-O-3.2's and ICCC-3's own authority, contract §0.7, registrar item §11.1); /0 benign cystic nephroma (including mixed epithelial and stromal tumour and paediatric DICER1 cystic nephroma, all synonyms/related terms on 8959/0 in icdo32.sqlite) is a behaviour_exclusion; /1 cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma is a behaviour_exclusion whose reason must say the case is outside the group's behaviour declaration, never that it is not a tumour — SIOP puts it in the low-risk group (Vujanić 2002, Table I, p. 81); a cystic Wilms tumour (cystic change within a true nephroblastoma, not a cystic nephroma) is 8960/3. icdo_term strings verified against icdo32.sqlite 22 Sep 2026: 8959/0 Preferred 'Benign cystic nephroma'; 8959/1 Preferred 'Cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma'.

options.label: Malignant cystic nephroma — a cystic renal tumour with malignant epithelial and/or stromal elements described, distinct from a nephroblastoma with cystic change
options.reason: Malignant cystic nephroma. ICD-O-3.2 carries 8959/3 and ICCC-3 Group VI admits it at behaviour 3; WHO 2022 Table 1 lists no entity at this code and behaviour, which is recorded for the registrar and does not block coding it here (contract §0.7).

options.label: Benign cystic nephroma, mixed epithelial and stromal tumour, or paediatric (DICER1) cystic nephroma — a cystic mass lined by bland epithelium with no malignant component described

behaviour_exclusion.reason: Benign cystic nephroma (which includes mixed epithelial and stromal tumour and the DICER1-associated paediatric cystic nephroma) is coded 8959/0. ICCC-3 Group VI admits behaviour 3 only, so it is not a registrable cancer in this group and no Group VI code is emitted for it. This case is outside the group's behaviour declaration, not outside the registry — record the finding and refer the case to the registrar.

options.label: Cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma — a multiloculated cystic tumour whose septa contain immature nephrogenic (primitive metanephric) elements

behaviour_exclusion.reason: Cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma is coded 8959/1. ICCC-3 Group VI admits behaviour 3 only, so no Group VI code is emitted for it. This case is outside the group's behaviour declaration and belongs with the registrar — it is a real, SIOP low-risk paediatric diagnosis, not a finding that this is not a tumour.

options.label: Cystic Wilms tumour — a nephroblastoma (triphasic or other Wilms morphology) with cystic change, distinct from a cystic nephroma
options.reason: A nephroblastoma with cystic change is still a nephroblastoma. Recorded as Nephroblastoma, NOS (8960/3), not as a cystic nephroma code.
options.coding_note: satisfies_tests ['Imaging'] added for the same reason as rn_histology's nephroblastoma option: reached by histology alone, and 8960's entry requires Imaging and Histology both.

options.label: Report describes a cystic renal mass but does not clearly state which of the above

nodes.step_label: Immunohistochemistry — rhabdoid / medullary / clear cell sarcoma fork
nodes.question: Tick each marker's result as the report states it, and record the sickle-cell status below.
nodes.hint: SMARCB1 (INI1) loss is the defining finding for BOTH rhabdoid tumour of the kidney and renal medullary carcinoma / SMARCB1-deficient carcinoma — loss alone never chooses between them; age and sickle-cell status do. WT1 is the discriminator the morphology cannot supply: positive points to blastemal Wilms tumour, negative supports clear cell sarcoma of the kidney. BCOR nuclear positivity is highly sensitive and specific for clear cell sarcoma of the kidney on its own (Aldera & Pillay 2020, pp. 121-122) — cyclin D1 and NGFR are sensitive but not specific and do not by themselves confirm it. Sickle-cell trait points at two different tumours, not one: renal medullary carcinoma and ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma both have a recognised association with it (Argani 2021), so ALK is tested alongside SMARCB1 in that context. Collecting duct carcinoma RETAINS SMARCB1 (INI1) nuclear expression and is a diagnosis of exclusion, reached only after fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma, renal medullary carcinoma, and a metastasis from another primary have been excluded (Trpkov 2021) — if SMARCB1 is retained here, evaluate this case through the carcinoma differential instead. 'Unknown' sickle-cell status is not the same as a negative test and must be recorded as its own state; in this registry it will often be the modal answer.
nodes.coding_note: Non-negotiable per task brief and build contract §4.3, §4.5, §4.6. Panel: SMARCB1 (INI1) loss, WT1, BCOR, ALK — four markers, each named in at least one resolution_logic rule's positive[] array (task brief engine fact 2; a rule keying only off 'when' with no marker renders nothing, the Group 4 defect). SMARCB1 loss is modelled as its OWN marker, 'SMARCB1 (INI1) loss', with 'Positive' meaning loss is demonstrated — not as a 'negative' requirement on a marker named 'SMARCB1 (INI1)' — because a negative[] requirement is satisfied by an untested marker as well as a confirmed-negative one (app.js markerOff()), and the age/sickle-conditioned rules must fire only on a CONFIRMED loss, never on an untested stain. sickle_cell_status is captured upstream, at rn_sickle_status (a small document_inventory node inserted before this one) — not via test_result_states, whose states are a closed, test-outcome vocabulary (positive/negative/not_done/etc., checked by build/build_database.py) with no room for 'trait' or 'disease' (an earlier authoring pass used test_result_states here and the build correctly rejected it). primary_site is captured 'C64.9' on every rn_document_inventory option (this whole tree is entered for a kidney mass) and read here by the rhabdoid rule's own 'when', because check_group6_8963_topography requires the 8963 terminal itself to gate on topography rather than relying on the tree's scope alone (contract §3.1). Cyclin D1 and NGFR (Aldera & Pillay 2020) are deliberately NOT built as resolution_logic markers: they are 'sensitive but not entirely specific' on the source's own wording, and a rule resolving 8964/3 on them alone would overstate the evidence BCOR alone already carries (task brief standing rule; Group 6 build contract epigraph). Rule order below satisfies task brief engine fact 4 (rules carrying 'when' precede unconditioned ones) and engine fact 6 (behaviour_exclusion / morphology_code mutual exclusivity — not applicable here, no option carries both). Sources: Sredni ST & Tomita T, Pediatric and Developmental Pathology 2015;18(1):49-58 (rhabdoid); Trpkov K, et al., Modern Pathology 2021;34(7):1392-1424, p. 1407 (medullary/RCCU-MP, haemoglobinopathy 'essential' per Trpkov); Moch H, et al., European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, §2.4 (haemoglobinopathy 'not a prerequisite', later document, group baseline — latest wins); Kanakaraj J, et al., Urologic Oncology 2024;42(7):211-219; Argani P, Genes, Chromosomes and Cancer 2021;60(3):219-227 (ALK/sickle trait); Aldera AP & Pillay K, Archives of Pathology & Laboratory Medicine 2020;144(1):119-123, pp. 121-122 (BCOR/cyclin D1/NGFR panel, WT1-negative discriminator).

marker_groups.group_label: Rhabdoid / medullary carcinoma / clear cell sarcoma / renal cell carcinoma differential

resolution_logic.reason: ALK rearrangement confirmed by immunohistochemistry or FISH in a child ten years or older with sickle-cell trait or disease. Sickle-cell trait is associated with both renal medullary carcinoma and ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma (Argani 2021) — this finding is specific to the latter. Recorded as ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma (8311/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: satisfies_tests as generous as rn_carcinoma_molecular's own ALK option, for the same reason: a positive finding by either modality is sufficient on its own (Cajaiba 2018) and 8311 requires all four of Histology/IHC/Cytogenetics-FISH/Molecular-PCR in its generated entry.

resolution_logic.reason: SMARCB1 (INI1) nuclear expression lost, in a child ten years or older with sickle-cell trait or disease. Recorded as Medullary carcinoma, NOS (8510/3), which on WHO 2022 Table 1 also carries SMARCB1-deficient medullary-like and undifferentiated renal cell carcinoma.

SMARCB1 (INI1) nuclear expression lost, in a child under five with a confirmed kidney (C64.9) primary — the typical rhabdoid tumour of the kidney age window. Recorded as Rhabdoid tumor, NOS (8963/3). 8963 at a CNS or other soft-tissue site belongs to a different ICCC-3 group entirely, which is why the site is confirmed on this rule, not assumed from the tree's own scope.

WT1 nuclear positivity is the discriminator morphology alone cannot supply between blastemal Wilms tumour (WT1 positive) and clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (WT1 negative, Aldera & Pillay 2020). Reclassified as Nephroblastoma, NOS (8960/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: satisfies_tests ['Imaging'] added: reached via histology, and 8960's entry requires Imaging and Histology both in diagnostic_tests_required — without this the engine would print a false 'Imaging would yield a more specific code' line on an IHC-confirmed case (same defect as rn_histology's nephroblastoma option, found driving this branch in the browser).

resolution_logic.reason: BCOR nuclear positivity is highly sensitive and specific for clear cell sarcoma of the kidney in the paediatric renal differential on its own (Aldera & Pillay 2020, pp. 121-122). Recorded as Clear cell sarcoma of kidney (8964/3).

SMARCB1 (INI1) nuclear expression is lost, but the age and sickle-cell context matches neither the rhabdoid tumour window (under 5) nor the renal medullary carcinoma window (10 or older, with sickle-cell trait or disease). Trpkov 2021 (p. 1407) treats haemoglobinopathy as an essential diagnostic criterion for renal medullary carcinoma; Moch 2022 (§2.4), the later document and this group's baseline, treats it as not a prerequisite and places the SMARCB1-deficient tumour without a documented haemoglobinopathy on the same code. This build does not resolve that disagreement on its own authority. Recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) — a SMARCB1-deficient malignant renal tumour is present — pending the registrar's coding decision between renal medullary carcinoma (8510/3) and rhabdoid tumour of the kidney (8963/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: satisfies_tests ['Imaging'] added: 8000's generated entry requires only Imaging, a weaker bar than the histology-plus-IHC evidence this branch actually rests on, so it is trivially exceeded rather than genuinely outstanding.

nos_fallback.name: Neoplasm, malignant
nos_fallback.reason: None of SMARCB1 (INI1) loss, WT1 positivity, BCOR positivity, or an ALK rearrangement was demonstrated. 8000/3 is the honest ceiling pending a fuller immunohistochemical panel or expert pathology review. If SMARCB1 (INI1) is specifically RETAINED, consider collecting duct carcinoma (8319/3) — a diagnosis of exclusion after fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma, renal medullary carcinoma, and a metastasis from another primary are excluded (Trpkov 2021) — and evaluate this case through the carcinoma differential instead.

nodes.question: What does the histology report state about this renal carcinoma's architecture?
nodes.hint: Code from the report's own stated architecture. Collecting duct carcinoma is a diagnosis of exclusion — do not select it unless the report (or your own review) has excluded fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma, renal medullary carcinoma, and a metastasis from another primary, and SMARCB1 (INI1) is documented as retained.
nodes.coding_note: Leaf codes per build contract §0.3 ('the renal-carcinoma leaves'), terms verified against icdo32.sqlite 22 Sep 2026: 8310/3 Preferred 'Clear cell adenocarcinoma, NOS' (Related 'Clear cell renal cell carcinoma, NOS'); 8260/3 Preferred 'Papillary adenocarcinoma, NOS' (Related 'Papillary renal cell carcinoma'); 8317/3 Preferred 'Renal cell carcinoma, chromophobe type'; 8319/3 Preferred 'Collecting duct carcinoma' (Synonym 'Bellini duct carcinoma'), ihc_markers_required ['SMARCB1 (INI1)'] on the generated entry — this option's own wording requires the clerk to affirm SMARCB1 retention, so it declares satisfies_tests ['IHC'] rather than leaving IHC outstanding; 8316/3 Preferred 'Cyst-associated renal cell carcinoma' (Related 'Tubulocystic renal cell carcinoma', 'Acquired cystic disease-associated renal cell carcinoma'); 8480/3 Preferred 'Mucinous adenocarcinoma' (Related 'Mucinous tubular and spindle cell carcinoma'). Papillary renal cell carcinoma — papillary architecture with fibrovascular cores
Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma — large cells with pale, reticulated cytoplasm and perinuclear haloes

Collecting duct carcinoma (Bellini duct carcinoma) — infiltrative tubulopapillary carcinoma centred in the renal medulla, high-grade, with a desmoplastic stroma, SMARCB1 (INI1) nuclear expression RETAINED, and fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma, renal medullary carcinoma, and a metastasis from another primary all excluded
options.reason: Collecting duct carcinoma is a diagnosis of exclusion, reached only once fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma, renal medullary carcinoma, and metastasis from another primary are excluded (Trpkov 2021). It is the one entity in this differential that RETAINS SMARCB1 (INI1) nuclear expression.

Mucinous tubular and spindle cell carcinoma

Eosinophilic, solid-and-cystic, or otherwise atypical carcinoma morphology not matching the above, a molecular alteration is already documented, or the architecture cannot be confidently classified on morphology alone

nodes.question: Which molecular or immunohistochemical finding does the report give?
nodes.hint: This is the most consequential single coding decision in the group (contract §0.5). Six of the seven molecularly defined renal cell carcinomas share 8311/3, not 8312/3: TFE3-rearranged, TFEB-altered, ELOC (TCEB1)-mutated, fumarate hydratase-deficient, HLRCC-associated, succinate dehydrogenase-deficient, and ALK-rearranged. 8312/3 is only for a carcinoma genuinely unclassified after this workup — select it only once the workup below is actually complete, never as a shortcut.
nodes.coding_note: Build contract §0.5, §4.5, §4.6. Workup order per Cajaiba MM, et al., Cancer 2018;124(16):3381-3389, p. 3387: TFE3 immunohistochemistry → TFE3/TFEB break-apart FISH → fusion-specific FISH → next-generation sequencing; a negative break-apart FISH does NOT overturn a positive TFE3 IHC with matching morphology, because NONO::TFE3 and RBM10::TFE3 rearrangements are inversions that break-apart probes miss. All 8311/3 outcomes below declare satisfies_tests covering the full IHC/Cytogenetics-FISH/Molecular-PCR list the generated entry requires, citing Cajaiba's own conclusion that IHC alone reliably detects these without further molecular studies — so nothing is left dangling as outstanding once one positive finding is in hand. WHO 2022 Table 1 (Moch 2022) assigns HLRCC-associated, TFE3-rearranged (MiT family translocation carcinoma), TFEB-altered, ELOC-mutated, fumarate hydratase-deficient, succinate dehydrogenase-deficient, and ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma all to 8311/3. cytogenetics_dropdown chosen over molecular_freetext for this node because app.js's resolveNode() for molecular_freetext reads only resolution_logic (a fixed pass-through), never options[] — confirmed by reading the engine before authoring — so a freetext node cannot be code-determining by what the clerk types; cytogenetics_dropdown's options[] IS read directly by advance(), which is what a genuinely code-defining, multi-finding workup needs (task brief; deviation recorded in the build report).

options.finding: TFE3 nuclear immunohistochemistry diffusely and strongly positive, with morphology and under-expression of epithelial markers consistent with a MiT-family translocation carcinoma
options.reason: TFE3 immunohistochemistry reliably detects MiT-family translocation carcinoma without the need for further molecular studies (Cajaiba 2018, p. 3387). Recorded as MiT family translocation carcinoma (8311/3), the commonest renal cell carcinoma subtype in this age group.

options.finding: TFE3 or TFEB break-apart FISH positive (rearrangement demonstrated)
options.reason: TFE3 or TFEB rearrangement confirmed by break-apart FISH. Recorded as MiT family translocation carcinoma (8311/3).

options.finding: Fusion-specific FISH or next-generation sequencing confirms a TFE3 gene rearrangement or a TFEB gene rearrangement, or identifies an ELOC (TCEB1) mutation
options.reason: Fusion-specific FISH or next-generation sequencing confirmed a TFE3 or TFEB rearrangement, or an ELOC (TCEB1) mutation. Recorded as 8311/3.
options.coding_note: This option exists for the case ordered after a break-apart FISH that did NOT itself show the rearrangement: NONO::TFE3 and RBM10::TFE3 are inversions that break-apart probes can miss (Cajaiba 2018, p. 3387), so a prior negative break-apart FISH does not exclude this option — the positive fusion-specific/sequencing result stands on its own.

options.finding: Fumarate hydratase (FH) immunohistochemistry shows loss, or a germline FH / hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) finding is documented
options.reason: Fumarate hydratase-deficient / HLRCC-associated renal cell carcinoma. WHO 2022 Table 1 assigns this to 8311/3, ICD-O-3.2's preferred term on the stem.

options.finding: Succinate dehydrogenase B (SDHB) immunohistochemistry shows loss
options.reason: Succinate dehydrogenase-deficient renal cell carcinoma. WHO 2022 Table 1 assigns this to 8311/3.

options.finding: ALK immunohistochemistry or FISH confirms an ALK rearrangement
options.reason: ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma, which also has a recognised association with sickle-cell trait (Argani 2021). WHO 2022 Table 1 assigns this to 8311/3.

options.finding: Full workup completed: TFE3 rearrangement not demonstrated, TFEB rearrangement not demonstrated, ELOC (TCEB1) mutation excluded, fumarate hydratase retained, succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) retained, and ALK rearrangement not demonstrated
options.reason: The molecular workup is complete: TFE3 rearrangement not demonstrated, TFEB rearrangement not demonstrated, ELOC (TCEB1) mutation excluded, fumarate hydratase retained, succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) retained, and ALK rearrangement not demonstrated. Recorded as Renal cell carcinoma, NOS (8312/3) — genuinely unclassified, not a shortcut around the workup.

nos_fallback.name: Renal cell carcinoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Molecular workup not completed or not yet resulted. 8312/3 is the honest ceiling until a specific molecularly defined entity is confirmed — do not infer 8311/3 without an actual positive finding (contract §0.5, both directions of the error are banned).
